SailPoint Technologies is a product-based IT company in the Identity and Access Management domain. We take pride in being Leaders in this domain, competing with big giants, enabling customers to efficiently manage digital identities securely and confidently.
Our identity governance platform answers three critical questions: Who has access to what? Who should have access to what? How is that access being used?
SailPoint helps organizations meet their service delivery requirements, improve internal controls, and manage the risks associated with access to sensitive data and applications across the enterprise.
Beyond great products, SailPoint has a great culture and a fun-loving work environment that is highly motivating and productive. We have the best identity team in the world working for us and are passionate about the power of identity. You can find more information about us at www.sailpoint.com.
SailPoint ’s Mainframe team develops Connectors for the three main security products: RACF, ACF2, and TSS. These connectors are offered as part of the SailPoint Identity Security Cloud and IdentityIQ products.
Using these Connectors, we provide our customers an efficient and reliable way to securely govern their Mainframe systems.
We have historically used zPDT environments to develop, validate, and support our connectors, and are now moving these environments to IBM’s cloud-hosted service that provides on-demand z/OS development and test environments (HDISV).

The System Programmer is responsible for providing support to critical internal mainframe-related infrastructure and system software. This is a professional-level position and requires strong execution and analytical abilities. This position is expected to interact and collaborate with Product Engineering and various groups within Information Technology. The candidate must have strong server, network,
communication, and analytical skills.

Responsible for the ongoing maintenance, security, and availability of Mainframe systems set up on IBM’s cloud-hosted service providing on-demand z/OS development and test environments.
Applies professional-level technical skill and judgement to provide non-routine technical support for computer / data center operations.
Installs, configures, upgrades, tunes, and troubleshoots the Mainframe z/OS operating system; applies PTFs / maintenance via SMP/E; performs Initial Program Loads (IPL); and tunes system parameters.
Installs and configures Mainframe security products such as RACF, ACF2, and TSS.
Monitors, tracks, and records system performance and utilization metrics.
Provides automation solutions for manual, repetitive tasks using scripting and configuration management systems.
Assists with the installation, configuration, and testing of newer product releases of the SailPoint Mainframe connector.
Improves the efficiency of, and helps standardize, current processes.
Determines and documents the root cause of an outage, its duration, and recommendations or steps to resolve issues.
Provides assistance as required in analysing trends and suggesting long-term and short-term improvements.
Assists in change management processes, implements change requests, and meets project deliverables within defined guidelines.
Ability to work after hours, including weekends and nights, when required.
Responds to general inquiries.
Requires a dynamic, hard-working individual with excellent inter-personal, oral, and written communication skills.
Capable of effectively communicating highly technical information to both technical and non-technical personnel.

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science / Engineering or equivalent relevant experience.
10+ years of solid experience working as a System Administrator in an enterprise environment.
Prior experience maintaining Mainframe z/OS environments and security products such as RACF, ACF2, and TSS.
Experience installing and configuring the Mainframe z/OS operating system, z/VM, z/PDT and HDISV.
Experience installing and configuring RACF, ACF2, or TSS.
Experience in REXX, JCL, and SMP/E.
Experience with TCP/IP programming, IBM/C, or SAS/C will be an added advantage.
Strong understanding of Linux, networking, firewalls, etc.
Strong ability to self-learn new technologies.
· Individual should be self-motivated with the ability to work independently.
Sound planning, organizational, and problem-solving skills.
Demonstrated ability to meet deadlines and commitments in an environment that requires multitasking among concurrent projects.

It all started with an idea at Block in 2013.

Initially built to take the pain out of peer-to-peer payments, Cash App has gone from a simple product with a single purpose to a dynamic ecosystem, developing unique financial products, including Afterpay/Clearpay, to provide a better way to send, spend, invest, borrow and save to our 50+ million monthly active customers.

We want to redefine the world’s relationship with money to make it more relatable, instantly available, and universally accessible.
Today, Cash App has thousands of employees working globally across office and remote locations, with a culture geared toward innovation, collaboration and impact. We’ve been a distributed team since day one, and many of our roles can be done remotely from the countries where Cash App operates. No matter the location, we tailor our experience to ensure our employees are creative, productive, and happy.

At Block, we strive to build the best financial products in the world. The Financial Platform Issuing team owns the card issuing platform that serves every Block brand — powering Cash App Card, the fourth-largest debit card program in the US, alongside Square Card and the new card programs Block launches next.
We run the full lifecycle of a card: issuance, fulfillment, and activation; real-time transaction authorization and processing across card networks; digital wallet provisioning; 3-D Secure authentication; clearing and settlement; and disputes. When a customer taps their card at a register, our systems decide the outcome in milliseconds, around the clock, in partnership with card networks and bank partners.
As a Staff Software Engineer on the Issuing server engineering team, you will bring deep card-network expertise to some of the most complex technical work on our roadmap. You will work alongside technical leads and cross functional teams, going deep where our platform meets the networks: specifications, protocols, certification, mandates, conformance, and production behavior.
This is a hands-on role. You will build systems and tooling, debug at the message level, and turn your network expertise into durable capabilities that other engineers can use. You will also work directly with the networks themselves — not only understanding what they require, but knowing where and how to influence outcomes for Block.
You Will
Be a deep technical expert on global card networks, helping Issuing teams interpret network specifications, message flows, certification requirements, mandates, and production behavior — and working directly with the networks to influence requirements, resolve ambiguity, and secure outcomes that matter for Block.
Lead complex, ambiguous engineering problems at the network boundary that span multiple teams, systems, or domains.
Partner with technical leads, program DRIs, and senior stakeholders to shape solutions where card-network requirements intersect with Block's issuing platform.
Stay deeply hands-on: write production code, build certification and conformance tooling, analyze network messages, review designs and code, and debug issues down to the protocol and field level.
Drive network certification and mandatory release cycles end to end, and translate network requirements into clear, pragmatic engineering decisions.
Establish shared frameworks, standards, tooling, and practices that make network expertise durable and enable teams to operate independently.
Raise the technical capability of engineers around you through design guidance, code reviews, mentorship, documentation, and clear technical judgment.
Apply AI-powered tools throughout the engineering lifecycle to improve velocity and quality, and help establish effective patterns for broader team use.
Share operational ownership of critical financial systems through on-call, incident response, and continuous improvements to reliability and correctness.
You Have
Deep, current expertise with at least one major card network, ideally Visa, including direct connectivity, ISO 8583, authorization and clearing flows, stand-in processing, specifications, certification, and mandate cycles.
Personally built, certified, or operated a live direct network connection — not only integrated through a processor.
Experience working directly with card networks to land concrete outcomes, such as rulings, exceptions, extensions, configuration changes, defect fixes, or certification outcomes.
Strong hands-on software engineering experience building and operating highly reliable financial or payments systems at scale.
A track record of leading technically complex, ambiguous work across team boundaries and influencing technical direction beyond your immediate area of ownership.
Experience creating durable technical leverage — frameworks, standards, tooling, architecture, or practices that other engineers and teams adopt.
Broad understanding of the card lifecycle, with depth in areas such as issuance and fulfillment, provisioning and activation, authorization, ledgering, clearing and settlement, reconciliation, disputes, or fraud.
Working knowledge of Mastercard and American Express, alongside deep expertise in at least one major network.
Fluency with AI-assisted engineering workflows and sound judgment in evaluating and applying AI-generated output.
Willingness to participate in an on-call rotation for critical financial systems.

SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

SpaceX is developing a satellite-to-mobile network to deliver ubiquitous cellular connectivity worldwide through the Starlink constellation. We are partnering with mobile network operators globally to provide direct-to-cell service, extending coverage to billions of existing cellular devices.

Starlink Mobile was designed to connect the unconnected, and this new product will greatly expand that mission by extending coverage to billions of existing cellular devices. Applications include connecting hikers in national parks, emergency responders, rural communities, remote sensors, and people in emergency situations.
